newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-LEADING LE MANS CAR ON FIRE NEAR FINISH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LEADING LE MANS CAR ON FIRE NEAR FINISH.

text.p: The works Porsche driven by German Ralf Kelleners caught fire when it was leading the Le Mans 24 Hours race with less than two hours to go on Sunday.
Kelleners, who shared the driving of the Porsche 911 GT1 with Frenchmen Yannick Dalmas, three times winner at Le Mans, and Emmanuel Collard, escaped from the blazing car unhurt.

A McLaren driven by Briton Andrew Scott -- with compatriot Ray Bellm and Masanori Sekiya of Japan -- also burst into flames some 20 minutes later when it was in fifth place at the same spot after the Mulsanne rise. Scott also escaped unhurt.

It was not immediately clear why the Porsche caught fire, but Dalmas had earlier warned that the engine was overheating, saying: "In the remaining hours there is going to be a very close, difficult fight... (The race has been) more of a sprint. We haven't let up since the start."
The lead passed to the Porsche prototype of last year's winning Joest stable driven by former Formula One racers Michele Alboreto of Italy and Stefan Johansson of Sweden with Dane Tom Kristensen.
Two other cars caught fire on Saturday evening and there were only 17 cars left from the entry of 48.
Another works Porsche driven by Frenchman Bob Wollek that had led a good part of the way crashed out of the race earlier on Sunday morning.
The Porsche 911 which Wollek was driving with German Hans Stuck and Thierry Boutsen of Belgium spun off at the Arnage bend with two thirds of the race run. Wollek was unhurt.
